approval_timeline.simple: Most residential trade permits are same-day through the PermitDallas portal if the application is complete and no plan review is triggered.

checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in TX
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
Panel schedule showing existing and proposed circuits
Wire gauge and breaker size for each new circuit
Electrical diagram or one-line drawing (required for panel upgrades)
Utility disconnect location marked on plans

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: The appropriate licensed contractor pulls each trade permit on the homeowner's behalf: a Texas-licensed electrical contractor/master electrician for the electrical permit, a TACL-licensed HVAC contractor for the mechanical permit, and the general contractor or owner-builder for the building permit if Dallas allows owner-builder filing for this scope. The contractor's license number must appear on the application where required.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to Dallas Development Services Department
response_body.city_contractor_registration: Dallas requires annual city contractor registration. Verify the registration is current before submitting any permit application, because an expired registration can block the permit silently. Renewal is yearly through Dallas Development Services.

common_mistakes: Submitting the permit application without verifying current Dallas contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block your application silently. Verify your registration is current BEFORE submitting.
Undervaluing the project on the permit application — Dallas uses a permit valuation system and low valuations can trigger audit or penalty fees.
Missing bedroom egress requirements on the new window — if the opening is too small or the sill is too high, the plan review will get kicked back.
Skipping AFCI protection on the new bedroom circuit(s) — bedrooms are a common inspection fail.
Assuming the HVAC extension can be done without a mechanical permit because it is only a duct add-on.

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through the Dallas PermitDallas portal: Dallas typically allows online inspection requests for permitted work; call (214) 948-4480 if the portal is unavailable or you need to confirm the inspection queue. Plan on at least 24 hours advance notice for inspection scheduling, and book rough-in inspections before drywall is installed.

inspections.description: Inspector checks: wall framing for the new bedroom, window opening size and egress compliance, insulation installation, fireblocking, drywall backing, and any structural changes from garage door infill or new openings.
inspections.timing: Before insulation is covered and before drywall is installed
Before insulation and drywall cover the wiring

inspections.description: Inspector checks: duct extension routing, supply/return sizing, register placement, insulation on ducts in unconditioned spaces, and proper airflow to the new bedroom.
inspections.timing: Before drywall closes the ceiling or walls

inspections.description: Inspector verifies: bedroom is finished as habitable space, window opens for emergency egress, outlets and switches are installed and working, HVAC serves the room, and all required smoke alarms are present.
inspections.timing: After all finishes, trim, devices, and HVAC are complete

pro_tips: Dallas PermitDallas can issue many residential trade permits same day, but garage conversions usually go faster if you upload a clean floor plan with dimensions and window sizes on the first submittal.
Use the correct project valuation up front. Dallas flags undervalued permits, and a realistic valuation reduces the chance of an audit or correction notice.
If the new bedroom window requires cutting a larger opening, show the header size and framing details on the plan set before you submit — that avoids a structural correction cycle.
Check your Dallas contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are one of the most avoidable rejection reasons.
If the garage slab or grading is being altered to match the new bedroom floor, ask Dallas whether a separate grading/drainage permit is needed before you start.
